base: The branch had no commits of its own and pointed at 5c182bd1, an older main from before #2170; this handoff commit sits on main 371d6c87, so the branch fast-forwards and the implementer starts on the code the plan cites.
summary: Opt-in ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS=1 (off by default; the hub's and Dispatch's grants refuse notifications.>). When on, a second bus.Connect client holds one core queue subscription notifications.> in its own group envoy-listener-live-<machine>; it drops subjects under notifications.role. or captured by the stream, reuses listenerDeliveryHandler with a no-retry liveDelivery mode, requires Topic == subject, and fans out. session.Deliverer reaches a session at the bridge (own machine), else its recorded Host, else today's fallback, with net.JoinHostPort. Subscribe refuses a port>0 registration with a malformed non-empty host. A denied live subscribe ends the start; /healthz reports live_topics and 503s on a dead live lane; shutdown drains it in 3 s (26 s total). The envoy-infra plugin gains ListenerConfig.SubscribeAllTopics and an optional subscribeAllTopics input on host:Listener and aws:WebhookListener; compose files set it; agent-infra's in-cluster listener sets it in the production record.

findings.finding: Host validation might reject an absent or empty host, breaking older plugins and the bridge fallback.
findings.answer: Only a non-empty host on a port>0 registration is checked; empty or absent is accepted and falls back as today; a port-0 host is stored unchecked (decision 5; api_test case with no host stays 200).

findings.finding: A connected client plus a valid core subscription does not prove NATS accepted it (nats.go v1.50.0 records a subscribe denial without closing the sub), and the handle returned at startup goes stale after recovery.
findings.answer: After SubscribeCore the live client flushes and a permission violation in LastError ends the start (exit 1) naming ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS; /healthz reads a new Client.CoreSubOK over the client's current subscription; a hub-grant natslive subtest proves the refusal and a bus recovery test proves the current handle (decision 6).

findings.finding: aws:WebhookListener renders its environment from explicit inputs, so a core field alone cannot enable it.
findings.answer: Both host:Listener and aws:WebhookListener gain an optional subscribeAllTopics input (default false), aws also through envoy-infra render webhook-listener-env --subscribe-all-topics; hub and Dispatch renderings stay byte-identical (decision 1, task 6).

findings.finding: Two separately bounded drains can exceed the 30 s grace period; the live lane publishes exceptions through the main client.
findings.answer: HTTP 10 s, then the live client drained in 3 s, then the main client 13 s: 26 s; the early shutdown on a failed bind drains it too; comments updated; a SIGTERM test with a blocked live delivery exits inside 30 s (decision 7).

findings.finding: The live adapter must keep the existing decode and wire/envelope validation before fanout.
findings.answer: The live wrapper filters by msg.Subject, then calls listenerDeliveryHandler with liveDelivery, which validates as today; the Topic == subject rule applies to the live lane only; TestALiveLaneDropsAnInvalidEnvelope (decision 3, task 5).

findings.finding: The two-listener test cannot use waitHealthy, since the second listener waits on the durable bind.
findings.answer: The live lane opens before /v1 and the durable bind and logs an INFO line once accepted; the test waits for that line in both outputs, publishes three events and counts three prompts (decision 2, task 5).

findings.finding: Exceptions on a non-stored topic go over core NATS (client.Publish routes by usesCoreTransport), and an ordinary HTTP failure on a general topic raises none, so the read-back test needs a real refusal.
findings.answer: The test provokes a delivery-mode refusal (payload {"delivery":{"mode":"btw"}} to a session advertising none), observes the exception prompt on a second session subscribed to notifications.envoy.exceptions.> through the live lane, and asserts exactly one exception on the bus (decision 3, task 5).

specDepartures.spec: The spec names the listener's own code and the corrected text as the change, and the production record as moving the in-cluster listener's image pin in theorem-labs/agent-infra; it leaves to the plan which input tells a listener whether its grant allows every notification topic.
specDepartures.plan: The input is an opt-in, ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS=1, off by default. The plan also changes the envoy-infra plugin (core.ListenerConfig.SubscribeAllTopics and an optional subscribeAllTopics input on host:Listener and aws:WebhookListener, plus envoy-infra render's flag), sets it in both compose files, and adds it to the in-cluster listener's environment in the same agent-infra change that moves the pin.
specDepartures.evidence: Nothing a listener reads tells ListenerPermissions (hub, Dispatch: infra/core/permissions.go:50-69,108-125) from HostPermissions (:150-156); NATS reports no grant and a probing subscribe is a refusal the live grant tests fail on; the hub cannot opt out without a cloud-config re-render that replaces its VM; the component-rendered and hand-written environments (infra/host/listener.go:106, infra/aws/rendering/listener.go:120, agent-infra envoy-cluster/listener.go:117-123) have no other way to set it. Every existing rendering, the hub's and Dispatch's included, stays byte-identical.

outcome.scope: Adds the envoy-infra plugin's ListenerConfig field and optional subscribeAllTopics inputs on host:Listener and aws:WebhookListener, the two compose files, and one environment variable in the agent-infra change the production record already needs.
